course.title: Year 11 Preliminary Textiles and Design
course.project: Two Preliminary textile projects: Project 1 Design; Project 2 Properties and Performance

syllabus.title: Textiles and Design Stage 6 Syllabus
syllabus.mandatory_from: Current syllabus for 2026; replacement in development

timetable.representation: Indicative two-hour planning blocks; local timetable conversion TTC-01

outcomes.statement: describes the elements and principles of design and uses them in a variety of applications
identifies the functional and aesthetic requirements and features of a range of textile items
demonstrates the use of a variety of communication skills, including computer-based technology
develops competence in the selection and use of appropriate manufacturing techniques and equipment
manages the design and manufacture of textile projects
identifies properties of a variety of fabrics, yarns and fibres
justifies the selection of fabrics, yarns and fibres for end-uses
identifies and selects textiles for specific end-uses based on analysis of experimentation
examines the status of the Australian Textile, Clothing, Footwear and Allied Industries within the global context
investigates the range of career options in design, consumerism, manufacturing and retail sectors of the Australian Textile, Clothing, Footwear and Allied Industries
identifies and appreciates the factors that contribute to the quality and value of textiles in society

periods.student_work: Teach Module 1 section 'Design purpose, users and requirements'; students view the design lens and complete the 10-question check.
periods.evidence: Saved written response and Folio Card 1; P1.2
syllabus_content: Functional and aesthetic design; user, purpose, context and factors determining appropriate design.

periods.student_work: Teach 'Elements of design'; model evidence-based analysis; students complete the video prompt and 10-question check.
periods.evidence: Written analysis and Folio Card 2; P1.1
syllabus_content: Line/direction, shape/size, texture, colour/value applied across textile applications.

periods.student_work: Teach 'Principles of design'; compare examples; students complete the video prompt and 10-question check.
periods.evidence: Supported judgement and Folio Card 2; P1.1
syllabus_content: Proportion, balance, rhythm, emphasis, contrast/harmony and unity.

periods.student_work: Model the Design-analysis studio. Students analyse one textile item, improve the response and save the evidence.
periods.evidence: Completed activity plus Folio Cards 1-2; P1.1, P1.2
syllabus_content: Describe and analyse elements and principles; identify functional and aesthetic requirements.

periods.student_work: Teach with the completed Module 2 theory, checks and applied-practice activity.
syllabus_content: Functional and aesthetic design across apparel, furnishings, costume, textile arts and non-apparel.

periods.student_work: Model how environmental sustainability and manufacturing techniques shape a design response.
syllabus_content: Factors determining appropriate design; role of design in meeting functional and aesthetic requirements.

periods.student_work: Students compare inspiration sources and explain how a concept changes through feedback and constraints.
syllabus_content: Generate, communicate, select and evaluate design ideas for a Preliminary textile project.

periods.student_work: Students record the user, purpose, requirements and one developed design direction in Folio Card 3.
periods.evidence: Folio Card 3 checkpoint; P1.1, P1.2, P2.1
syllabus_content: Apply elements and principles; select, analyse and record design idea development.

periods.student_work: Teacher explains approved pattern information, symbols, measurements and quality checkpoints; use the completed site module.
syllabus_content: Manufacturing methods; interpret, use and modify patterns for specific end-uses.

periods.student_work: Students prepare a teacher-approved order of work and quality checkpoints without inventing technical details.
periods.evidence: Approved plan and Folio Card 3; P2.1, P2.3
syllabus_content: Outline and justify project development and management steps; communicate production information.

periods.student_work: Teacher demonstrates the authorised technique and controls. Students practise under supervision and retain one labelled sample.
syllabus_content: Select and use manufacturing techniques appropriate to fabric and end-use.

periods.student_work: Students repeat or extend an authorised technique, check quality and record one improvement.
periods.evidence: Improved sample and feedback record; P2.2, P2.3
syllabus_content: Develop competence with appropriate manufacturing techniques and equipment.

periods.student_work: Teacher models object, fashion and production drawing conventions from authorised course sources.
syllabus_content: Graphical communication: object, fashion and industry production drawing specifications.

periods.student_work: Compare verbal, written, graphical and digital methods; students select a method for a defined audience.
syllabus_content: Criteria for effective verbal and written communication; communication-based technologies.

periods.student_work: Students create a teacher-approved drawing or annotated specification for Project 1.
periods.evidence: Communication evidence in Folio Card 3; P2.1
syllabus_content: Develop competence in graphically communicating design ideas using appropriate media.

periods.student_work: Run a short peer/teacher review. Students document one supported change and update their project plan.
syllabus_content: Communicate, evaluate and modify design ideas; manage time and resources.

periods.student_work: Check approved brief, design evidence, pattern, resources and sequence. Students identify the next authorised action.
syllabus_content: Manage project development; evaluate ideas; plan time and resources.

periods.student_work: Teacher demonstrates the approved stage. Students manufacture under supervision and complete clean-down.
periods.evidence: Progress photo/sample and teacher checkpoint; P2.2, P2.3
syllabus_content: Project construction using appropriate methods, techniques and equipment.

periods.student_work: Students continue the approved sequence, check accuracy and respond to feedback.
periods.evidence: Technique evidence in Folio Card 4; P2.2, P2.3
syllabus_content: Apply manipulative skills and manage the textile project.

periods.student_work: Students continue the approved sequence and record one quality issue or decision.
syllabus_content: Use appropriate manufacturing techniques; manage time and resources.

periods.student_work: Students complete the approved construction sequence and carry out teacher-directed quality checks.
syllabus_content: Complete and evaluate a Preliminary textile project using appropriate methods.

periods.student_work: Students photograph the authorised result, compare it with requirements and record a realistic improvement.
periods.evidence: Folio Card 6 evaluation; P1.2, P2.3, P4.1
syllabus_content: Evaluate ideas and project; substantiate conclusions with factual evidence.

periods.student_work: Teacher-led classification lesson using the approved properties booklet; use the completed site module.
syllabus_content: Natural, regenerated and synthetic fibre types and classifications.

periods.student_work: Explain monomer, polymer, amorphous and crystalline regions with verified diagrams.
syllabus_content: Molecular structure and its contribution to fibre properties.

periods.student_work: Compare surface and cross-sectional features, staple, filament and multifilament forms.
syllabus_content: Morphological structure and its contribution to fibre properties.

periods.student_work: Students choose one verified fibre example and justify an end use using structure and properties.
syllabus_content: Select fibres for specific end-uses using evidence about properties.

periods.student_work: Teach cotton origin, structure, processing, properties and end-use from approved sources.
syllabus_content: Properties of natural cellulosic fibre; cotton classification and performance.

periods.student_work: Teach wool origin, structure, processing, properties and end-use from approved sources.
syllabus_content: Properties of natural protein fibre; wool classification and performance.

periods.student_work: Compare viscose rayon, polyester, nylon, elastomeric and the required blends.
syllabus_content: At least one regenerated, three synthetic fibres and two fibre blends.

periods.student_work: Students justify one natural and one manufactured fibre or blend for contrasting end uses.
syllabus_content: Describe fibre properties and justify fibre selection for end-use.

periods.student_work: Compare staple-spun and filament construction and apply correct terminology.
syllabus_content: Spun staple and filament yarn structure and characteristics.

periods.student_work: Explain low/high twist and carded/combed or woollen/worsted distinctions.
syllabus_content: Twist level and spinning systems that affect yarn and fabric properties.

periods.student_work: Identify textured, slub, boucle and core-spun examples from verified sources or teacher samples.
syllabus_content: Textured and novelty yarn structures and characteristics.

periods.student_work: Students select one yarn structure and explain how it contributes to fabric behaviour.
periods.evidence: Folio Card 7 yarn record; P3.1, P3.2
syllabus_content: Identify yarn characteristics that affect fabric properties.

periods.student_work: Teach how yarn structure affects appearance, handle and comfort.
syllabus_content: Yarn aesthetic and comfort properties and their effect on fabric performance.

periods.student_work: Compare durability, strength and care demands using verified examples.
syllabus_content: Yarn durability, strength and care properties.

periods.student_work: Model a chain from fibre to yarn structure to fabric performance and end use.
syllabus_content: Interrelationship of yarn structure, yarn properties and fabric performance.

periods.student_work: Students justify a yarn selection for a specific textile end use using evidence.
syllabus_content: Demonstrate understanding of yarn properties when selecting fabrics for end-use.

periods.student_work: Teach warp, weft and selvedge, then compare plain, twill, satin, Jacquard, crepe and pile weaves.
syllabus_content: Woven fabric structure, terminology, types and classification.

periods.student_work: Teach course and wale, then compare the required knitted fabric types.
syllabus_content: Single, double, tricot, pile, lace and net knitted structures.

periods.student_work: Compare felt, web and film structures and link construction to likely performance.
syllabus_content: Non-woven fabric structures, classification and properties.

periods.student_work: Using teacher-approved samples and method, students identify structure and record evidence rather than appearance alone.
periods.evidence: Folio Card 7 sample record; P3.1, P3.2
syllabus_content: Identify fabric structures and describe properties affected by structure.

periods.student_work: Compare aesthetic, durability, comfort, dimensional stability and care properties.
syllabus_content: Fabric and fibre properties used when selecting fabrics for specific end-uses.

periods.student_work: Model an aim, variables, consistent method, results table and evidence-based conclusion without supplying an unapproved method.
syllabus_content: Use functional and aesthetic tests to record and evaluate results.

periods.student_work: Students prepare Folio Card 8 fields and a teacher-approved recording format before testing.
syllabus_content: Plan experimental procedures; communicate and record information.

periods.student_work: Teacher demonstrates the approved method and controls. Students test, record results and clean down under supervision.
periods.evidence: Results and observations in Folio Card 8; P3.1, P4.1
syllabus_content: Evaluate fabric properties using classroom testing procedures.

periods.student_work: Students analyse authorised test results and justify one fabric, yarn or fibre selection for the confirmed project.
syllabus_content: Make decisions about textiles using analysis of properties and experimental evidence.

periods.student_work: Teacher demonstrates the approved Bustier/Vest stage. Students work under supervision and complete clean-down.
syllabus_content: Project 2 construction using techniques appropriate to fabric and end-use.

periods.student_work: Students continue the approved sequence, check quality and record a supported decision.
periods.evidence: Teacher checkpoint and Folio Card 9; P2.1, P2.2, P2.3
syllabus_content: Apply manipulative and management skills; communicate and record information.

periods.student_work: Students complete the authorised item, collect product evidence and evaluate design, selection and manufacture.
periods.evidence: Completed Folio Card 9; P2.3, P3.2, P4.1
syllabus_content: Evaluate textile selection and project outcomes using factual evidence.

periods.student_work: Use current primary evidence to outline one ATCFAI sector and its development; use the completed site module.
syllabus_content: Role of textiles; sectors; development across the 19th, 20th and 21st centuries.

periods.student_work: Compare Australian industry participation with global markets and identify one current issue using dated sources.
syllabus_content: Contribution to local/global markets; issues, trends and future opportunities.

periods.student_work: Students investigate one current career pathway, required training and changing work context.
periods.evidence: Career profile for Folio Card 10; P5.2
syllabus_content: Current and future employment and training opportunities across ATCFAI sectors.

periods.student_work: Compare design, trademarks, fabric quality, legislation, assurance checks and control measures.
syllabus_content: Influences on quality; methods of quality assurance in the marketplace.

periods.student_work: Examine manufacturer/consumer roles and perceived, cultural and economic value.
syllabus_content: Factors contributing to quality and value across textile end-uses.

periods.student_work: Students build one sourced case analysis and record title, organisation, date and location.
syllabus_content: Investigate quality assurance and discuss factors contributing to textile value.

periods.student_work: Retrieve Design concepts, diagnose gaps and plan one supported response using command terms.
periods.evidence: Low-stakes check and response plan; P1.1-P2.3
syllabus_content: Design content from elements/principles through communication, manufacture and Project 1.

periods.student_work: Retrieve fibre, yarn, fabric, testing and selection concepts; correct misconceptions.
periods.evidence: Low-stakes check and response plan; P3.1, P3.2, P4.1
syllabus_content: Properties and Performance content; experimentation and end-use selection.

periods.student_work: Students connect design, textile performance and industry/value in unfamiliar examples.
syllabus_content: Integrated application of the three Preliminary areas of study.

periods.student_work: Students check Folio Cards 1-10, identify incomplete evidence and prepare a personal revision priority list.
periods.evidence: Folio completeness record and next-step plan; P1.1-P6.1
syllabus_content: Evaluate and communicate project, experimental and industry evidence across the course.
